---
title: "XLSForm integration"
---

## Standard execution boundary

The example workbooks use the MethodMesh execution action:

```text
com.example.methodmesh.EXECUTE_METHOD
```

A method is selected with `method_id`, and arguments are supplied through named `input_*` values.

Example:

```text
com.example.methodmesh.EXECUTE_METHOD(
  method_id='sensor.read',
  input_device_id=${config_device_id},
  input_sensor_read_mode=${config_read_mode},
  return_mode='flat'
)
```

## Recommended group pattern

Use a `begin_group` row with `body::intent` for the execution call. Put read-only output questions inside that group so MethodMesh can return named values directly.

```text
begin_group   methodmesh_result   Run MethodMesh   body::intent=<call>
text          result_status       Status           read_only=yes
text          result_value        Result           read_only=yes
end_group
```

## Input naming

Capability inputs use the `input_*` namespace. Keep input names explicit and stable.

Examples:

```text
input_device_id
input_sensor_read_mode
input_target_latitude
input_verification_method
```

## Return modes

Many examples request:

```text
return_mode='flat'
```

Flat output is convenient for XLSForm fields. Where a result is complex, retain a JSON field as well as the most useful flattened values.

## Status handling

Do not infer success merely because Android returned to ODK Collect. Test the explicit status field.

A form should normally handle:

- succeeded or completed;
- cancelled;
- failed;
- invalid input;
- provider unavailable;
- permission denied;
- timeout.

The exact values are capability-specific and are documented on the relevant page.

## Complete examples

The supplied workbooks are copied into the [example catalogue](examples/index.qmd). Each capability page links to the examples that correspond to it.
